content:
alex: Heads up — we're seeing a weird packing pattern in eu-west-1 GPUs. Small inference pods are spread across 40 nodes leaving 20 nodes half-used, then large fine-tuned jobs can't schedule and trigger evictions.

maya: Yep noticed that too. Eviction spikes around 02:00 UTC yesterday, lots of NACKs from the scheduler.

sourav: Quick check: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep Evicted` shows ~18 evicted in the last 3 hours, mostly PS/worker-role jobs.

alex: Log sample from scheduler logs: ```I0314 01:58:12.345678 1 scheduler_predicates.go:123] Fit failed: Insufficient memory on node gpu-node-74 for pod inference-large-2026``` Notably GPU alloc looked free but CPU/memory blocked packing.

jess: My hunch is fragmentation from per-pod requests being conservative and topologySpreadConstraints forcing cross-node distribution. We tried to avoid noisy-neighbor latencies but now it's killing binpacking.

maya: Options: 1) relax spread constraints for low-priority inference, 2) introduce a nightly defrag job (descheduler), 3) create "soft-pools" of smaller nodes reserved for small pods to pack them together. Thoughts?

sourav: +1 for descheduler run with RemoveDuplicates and LowNodeUtilizationPlugin, but need eviction SLA — don't want to evict live traffic during day. Run during low-traffic window and gradually push.

alex: Prototype descheduler config I tested: ```yaml apiVersion: "descheduler/v1alpha1" kind: DeschedulerPolicy strategies: RemoveDuplicates: {} LowNodeUtilization: {thresholds: {targetUtilization: {cpu: 50, memory: 60}} }``` Ran in staging and freed up ~12 GPUs for large jobs.

jess: Nice. Two caveats: 1) evictions create extra startup/training cost (more network egress + checkpoint reloads) and 2) multi-az constraints — we can't defrag across AZs due to latency/affinity. Need AZ-aware policy.

maya: For AZs we can run descheduler per-az and add nodeSelector `topology.kubernetes.io/zone`. Also propose tagging latency-sensitive pods with `nodeAffinity: preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` to prefer same-az.

alex: Could also add a binpack admission webhook that tries to co-locate small inference replicas onto nodes with existing small-pod labels, fallback to scheduling normally if none. This reduces fragmentation over time.

jess: What about cost/regional constraints? eu-west-1 has spot pools and dedicated reserved nodes. Spots bounce more and increase fragmentation — maybe pin large jobs to reserved/dedicated nodes and allow small jobs on spot.

sourav: Agreed. We can set nodeAffinity for big jobs `nodeSelector: reserved=true` and use a lower-preference affinity for spot pools. That should reduce preemptions and evictions.

maya: Action items: (1) schedule a descheduler nightly run in eu-west-1 between 03:00-04:00 UTC with AZ-scoped policy (maya) (2) create a small-node soft-pool tag + admission hint to binpack small pods (alex) (3) add nodeAffinity for large reserved jobs and mark spot pools (jess) (4) monitor eviction counts + cost delta (sourav).

alex: I'll open PR for the descheduler job and a minimal webhook prototype.

deploy-bot: descheduler-job (eu-west-1) scheduled: cron */30 3-4 * * * — created by alex — run window set to low-traffic — /ping for rollback.

maya: Cool — let's roll this out to canary cluster first and watch metrics (evictions, packing efficiency, token latency). If no regressions after 48h, promote. :thumbsup:

jess: Also add a metric for node fragmentation: fraction of nodes with <40% GPU utilization but >20% CPU/memory usage. That should capture this specific symptom.

sourav: I'll add a Grafana panel and alert for >10 fragmented nodes for >2h.

alex: Thanks all — will link PR and staging run results here once ready.
